messages.author: 3d0e230fded30495
messages.subject: Diagnostic plots
parts:
Hello,

I'm not sure how to interpret diagnostic plots for two models (for two morphological structures). Upper plots are when I used CS as a covariate and below them is when I used log CS. I can see they're not ideal, but I'm not sure if they reveal major problems, like gross violation of the homoscedasticity assumption.

Also, I was wondering if Procrustes ANOVA and np-MANOVA are the same things? I'm pretty sure they are, but I don't quite get why in some papers they use both terms. At some parts it is said - for this analysis we performed P. ANOVA and in others - for this analysis we performed np-MANOVA. Personally, I would use just one term so I'm not sure if I'm missing something.

Thank you

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Diagnostic plots
parts:
Ellen,

 

The typical use for size measures is logCS, and I would recommend that here also. As for Procrustes ANOVA and np-MANOVA, as they are typically implemented they are the same. The latter term is more general, as it may be used with any type of high-dimensional data, not just shape coordinates.

 

Dean
